name: ExprForge
comment: Mirrors expr.js's own tokenizeSegment exactly (see that file's header comment) -- the same source of truth playground/src/tools/playground/exprForgeMode.ts's CodeMirror mode already follows, so this and the playground's own highlighting never drift apart. Grammar surface is small and fully regex-lexable, per docs/editor-support-spec.md's own Phase 1a scope: '#' comments, numbers (incl. '.5', '1e-9'), the 'let'/'return'/'fn'/'macro' keywords (contextual in the real parser -- only special at specific positions -- but colored as keywords unconditionally here, same simplification exprForgeMode.ts already makes), identifiers, and the fixed operator/punctuation set.

comments.comment: '#' runs to end of line -- exprsegment.js's own rule, no block-comment syntax exists in the grammar.
comments.name: comment.line.number-sign.exprforge

numbers.comment: 123, 123.45, .5, 1e-9, 1E+9 -- same shape as expr.js's readNumber. Tried before #accessor below so a leading '.' followed by a digit is claimed here first; '.' followed by anything else (field access, e.g. b.rx) correctly falls through instead.
numbers.name: constant.numeric.exprforge

keywords.comment: Contextual in the real parser (statement-start / signature-start position only, see fn.js) -- colored unconditionally here, same simplification exprForgeMode.ts already makes for highlighting purposes. 'fn'/'macro' are the mandatory leading keywords loadExprSource()'s stricter multi-definition grammar requires (see fn.js's requireExportKeyword mode); a lone fn`...` call never requires or recognizes them as anything but ordinary identifiers, but coloring them the same way here regardless is harmless and consistent.
keywords.name: keyword.control.exprforge

function-calls.comment: An identifier immediately followed by '(' -- primitive or macro/extern call, not distinguished here (same 'defer name resolution to the real parser/emitter' precedent call() itself follows, see ast.js).
function-calls.name: entity.name.function.exprforge

operators.comment: Two-character comparisons before their one-character prefixes -- same ordering rule expr.js's own tokenizer follows.
operators.name: keyword.operator.exprforge

accessor.comment: Postfix '.' field access (b.rx, chainable a.b.c) -- see expr.js's parsePostfix.
accessor.name: punctuation.accessor.exprforge
